subtopics.title: Two Norths and the Angle Between Them

questions.question: Magnetic declination is:
options: The angle between true north and magnetic north
The distance between the two poles
The height of the magnetic pole
The time difference between two time zones

questions.question: In South Africa, the compass needle points:
options: West of true north, so declination is stated as west of true north

questions.question: The declination note in a map's margin gives which three facts?
options: The sheet name, the scale and the contour interval
The latitude, the longitude and the altitude
The declination in a stated year, the mean annual change, and the direction of that change
The magnetic bearing, the true bearing and the grid bearing

questions.question: How many minutes of arc make one degree?
The declination was 18°19' west in 2014 with a mean annual change of 5' westward. The difference in years to 2025 is:
Eleven years of change at 5' westward per year gives a total change of:
The change is westward and the declination is already west of true north, so you must:
options: Add the change, because the angle is growing
Subtract the change, because the angle is shrinking

questions.question: 18°19' plus 55' equals 18°74', which must be written as:
options: 19°14' west of true north, because 60 minutes carry into one degree

questions.question: The iron rule of the area calculation is:
options: Multiply the map centimetres first, then convert the square centimetres
Convert each measured distance to real ground units first, then multiply

questions.question: On a 1:10 000 orthophoto, a measured length of 3,5 cm converts to:
With length 350 m and breadth 180 m, the area of the demarcated feature is:
On a 1:50 000 topographic sheet, a block of 4 cm by 3 cm has an area of:

subtopics.title: Marks, Traps and the Answer Line

questions.question: An answer of 18°74' west of true north loses the answer mark because:
options: Any minute count of sixty or more must carry into degrees
Declination is never measured in minutes

questions.question: Which declination answer is complete?
The square-centimetre dead end in area questions means:
options: Multiplying the paper centimetres first and converting afterwards, which linear scale factors cannot fix
Using the formula for a triangle

questions.question: The declination correction and the area calculation both stand on which earlier skill?
options: Converting a measured map distance into real ground distance using the scale

subtopics.title: The Compass That Tells a Small Lie

questions.question: In the two-arrows picture, the wedge of angle between the map's arrow and the needle's arrow is:
options: The magnetic declination — the size of the compass's lie

questions.question: The wedge grows by a few minutes every year because:
options: The magnetic pole wanders as the deep Earth churns
True north moves with the seasons

questions.question: To walk a direction taken off the map, the translation sentence is:
options: True bearing equals magnetic bearing plus declination west
Magnetic bearing equals true bearing plus the declination, where declination is west
Magnetic bearing equals true bearing minus the declination, where declination is west

questions.question: Angle minutes work like clock minutes because:
options: Both are measured with a stopwatch
An angle takes one minute to measure
Sixty of them make one whole — one degree, or one hour

questions.question: Just as 74 minutes past six is 14 minutes past seven, 18 degrees and 74 minutes rolls over to:
If a margin note said the annual change was EASTWARD on a westerly declination, you would:
options: Add the change, because all changes are added
Subtract the change, because the needle is swinging back towards true north and the lie shrinks

subtopics.title: The Rugby Field in Your Answer Book

questions.question: The tiling order of operations for map area is:
options: Convert one side only, then multiply
Convert the length, convert the breadth, then multiply

questions.question: On the orthophoto, 1,8 cm of measured breadth un-shrinks to:
A rugby field is roughly 100 m by 70 m, so 7 000 m². The 63 000 m² block is therefore about:
options: Nine rugby fields — a sensible size for a demarcated map feature

questions.question: Why can the paper centimetres not be multiplied first and converted afterwards?
options: The shrinking happened to each side separately, so each side must be un-shrunk separately before multiplying
Centimetres are too small to multiply
Multiplication only works on whole numbers
